text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a ~3x p90 latency spike on prod cluster-7 in the last hour. Trigger seems tied to long-context (>32k) sessions. KV cache is paging under memory pressure and I see a flurry of evictions. Trace attached.
maria: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] KV_PAGE evict page_id=0x7f2a req_id=43721 policy=FIFO reason=mem_pressure reuse_hint=0
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] KV_LOAD miss prefix=conv_0x1a cost=120ms
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] LATENCY req=43722 p95=1.2s (baseline 400ms)
```
alex: Can you drop the kv stats and /proc/meminfo for that host? Any recent config rollouts or model swaps? :thinking_face:
maria: Model is redwood/xxl-16k-q4f; no model rollout. kv stats (snippet):
```
kv.entries: 1_220_311
kv.pages.total: 248
kv.pages.free: 4
kv.used_bytes: 49_200_432_128
kv.fragmentation_pct: 18.7
kv.evictions.last_5m: 12_432
kv.reuse_ratio.1h: 0.37
```
Notice high fragmentation and reuse_ratio ~0.37 — heavy reuse but still lots of evictions.
kevin: Wait, why is policy=FIFO in the logs? Our default under pressure should prefer LRU tokens. @sasha did we enable any fallback heuristics?
sasha: We rolled out a change yesterday: a page-scan timeout that, when tripped, switches the eviction chooser to a fast FIFO fallback to avoid long scanning stalls. It was meant to reduce cpu jitter. Seems like the heuristic is triggering on these long-context workloads and FIFO is thrashing hot prefixes.
perf-bot: profiling snapshot (hot paths):
```
kv_page_fault: 62% compact_page
kv_page_fault: 18% relink_lru
kv_page_fault: 10% page_scan_loop
kv_page_fault: 5% page_writeback
```
Heap backtrace: compact_page -> scan_segment -> evict_fifo_fast
```
alex: If FIFO is evicting recently used but high-reuse prefixes, we get cache misses that force recompute/decoder loads and huge tail latency. We should repro with a microbench mixing long append-only sessions and random short requests.
maria: Repro command I'm using locally against a perf cluster:
```
./tools/kv_bench --hosts cluster7 --pattern long-reuse --ctx 32768 --rate 1200
```
Repro reliably shows p95 regression and many FIFO evict logs.
kevin: I repro locally. FIFO fallback is too blunt for this workload. I hacked a tiny tie-break: if page.recent_access == true then deprioritize for FIFO eviction. Quick diff:
```
- if (policy == FIFO) evict(page);
+ if (policy == FIFO) {
+   if (page.recent_access) keep(page);
+   else evict(page);
+ }
```
This reduces repeated loads in my replay.
sasha: Alternative: prefer LRU when reuse_ratio > 0.3 (configurable threshold), or add a short grace window after a fault so newly-accessed pages aren't immediately eligible for FIFO. Concern: LRU maintenance CPU cost under high batching.
maria: Prod mitigation plan: set `kv.page_scan_timeout = 0` on cluster-7 to avoid switching to FIFO, and bump `kv.cache_limit` by +5% for now. I'll roll a canary to 10% of traffic.
deploy-bot: deploy started — canary cluster=cluster-7/zone-a image=r-inference@b3f8, config=kvcfg-2026-03-17-01. Rolling to 10%.
perf-bot: canary metrics (4m after): p95 latency down 28%, eviction_rate down 73%, reuse_ratio stable. Continuing to monitor.
alex: Nice work. Follow-ups: add a unit test for FIFO tie-break behavior, a microbenchmark in the perf-suite that reproduces this long-context reuse pattern, and a dashboard alert when fallback-to-fifo rate > 0.5% of evictions. Assigning kevin + sasha.
kevin: On it — I'll push a PR with the tie-break and a unit test. Will also run the perf-suite microbench overnight and post results.
sasha: I'll prototype the config flag (reuse_ratio threshold) and our telemetry for fallback rate. If the CPU delta is acceptable we can prefer LRU for reuse-heavy workloads.
maria: Thanks all. I'll leave the canary running for an hour then either roll forward or revert if we see regressions. :thumbsup:
